title: Tower category and adic coefficient datum
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and use the small skeleton and universes of its small pro-etale site $T_{\Proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a sheaf of rings $B_T$, modules mean sheaves of left modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define
$$\operatorname{Tow}_B(T)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\Mod(B_T)).$$
Here the positive integers form the poset category with a unique arrow $a\to b$ when $a\leq b$. Objects are strict inverse sequences and maps are compatible levelwise maps [def-weil-inverse-system]. This is a Grothendieck abelian category by [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck]. Kernels, cokernels and exactness are levelwise, and $\operatorname{ev}_n$ is exact [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Its extension to derived categories is termwise evaluation [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated].

Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ an ideal, and $P_n=A/I^n$ for $n\geq1$, using the powers and quotients of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume $A/I$ is torsion as an additive group (every element is killed by a positive integer), and every $P_n$ is finite as a set and perfect as an $A$-module placed in degree zero [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Give $P_n$ the discrete topology. Define $(P_n)_T$ by the coefficient presheaf and sheafification of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]: $U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P_n)$, where connected components carry the quotient topology and restriction is precomposition. For $b\geq a\geq1$ the quotient map $P_b\to P_a$ induces the map of these coefficient sheaves by postcomposition. Write $q_{b,a}$ for it. Postcomposition gives $q_{a,a}=1$ and $q_{c,a}=q_{b,a}q_{c,b}$.

Define the sheaf of commutative rings $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$: on each site object $U$ its sections are the compatible families in $\prod_n(P_n)_T(U)$, with pointwise operations and restrictions. Compatible families satisfy the sheaf gluing condition because each component does, so this is the actual limit sheaf with projections $\pi_n:A_T\to(P_n)_T$. In this node set
$$D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\Mod(A_T)),\qquad\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)=\operatorname{Tow}_{A_T}(T),$$
using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This convention uses the completed coefficient sheaf $A_T$; the same notation in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] uses the constant coefficient sheaf, and no identification of those two ambient categories is asserted here.

For a complex $C$ of $A_T$-modules, choose a K-flat resolution $Q C\to C$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For a K-flat complex $P$ define the strict tower of complexes $F(P)_n=P\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T$ with transitions $1\otimes q_{n+1,n}$; tensor is the termwise sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. All levels are regarded as $A_T$-modules by restriction of scalars along $\pi_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The differentials commute with the transitions, so this is a complex in $\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$.

Define $K\mapsto K_\bullet$ to be the left derived functor of this termwise tower construction, computed as $F(Q C)$ for any representative $C$ of $K$. Its existence and independence of the representative are provided by [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]: the termwise additive tower construction preserves shifts and cone complexes (tensor distributes over the two finite summands in the cone), hence gives an exact functor from the homotopy category to $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$. K-flat resolutions exist by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. A quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes is carried to a quasi-isomorphism at each level by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; because cohomology of towers is levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], it is carried to a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes. These verify both hypotheses of the resolving-class theorem. Functoriality is in the derived category; no strict functor from the derived category to chosen complex representatives is part of this definition.

Define the quotient-coefficient object by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]:
$$K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T\in D(\Mod((P_n)_T)).$$
The $n$-th evaluation of $K_\bullet$ lies in $D(\Mod(A_T))$ and is canonically the restriction of scalars of $K_n$ along $\pi_n$: both are computed by $Q C\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T$ with its $A_T$-action. Exactness of restriction follows from the underlying abelian sheaves, so its termwise derived functor is given by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The quotient-coefficient objects have normalization isomorphisms
$$K_b\otimes^L_{(P_b)_T}(P_a)_T\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a\quad(b\geq a).$$
Here is the explicit computation: if $P$ is K-flat over $A_T$, then $P\otimes_{A_T}(P_b)_T$ is K-flat over $(P_b)_T$, since for any acyclic $(P_b)_T$-complex $N$ its tensor with this complex is $P\otimes_{A_T}N$, which is acyclic after restricting scalars. Restriction preserves acyclicity because it does not change the underlying abelian sheaves. Thus the normalization is represented by the ordinary balancing isomorphism
$$ (P\otimes_{A_T}(P_b)_T)\otimes_{(P_b)_T}(P_a)_T\longrightarrow P\otimes_{A_T}(P_a)_T,\quad (x\otimes b)\otimes a\longmapsto x\otimes q_{b,a}(b)a,$$
with inverse $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. Balancing shows both composites are identities. The same formula for three quotients sends $((x\otimes c)\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes q_{c,a}(c)q_{b,a}(b)a$ along either composite. This proves the quotient cocycle. For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, applying either normalization followed by $f\otimes1$ or $(f\otimes1)\otimes1$ followed by normalization sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $f(x)\otimes q_{b,a}(b)a$; this proves naturality on K-flat complexes. These balanced section maps commute with restrictions and differentials and therefore induce maps of the sheafified tensor complexes. They descend through quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so the naturality and cocycle equalities hold in the derived categories independently of the resolution.

Stacks Tag 099M, in Section Tag 099L, gives the formula $K^\wedge=R\lim(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$ for a Noetherian constant coefficient ring on a site. It supplies context for the reduction tower, rather than a definition or comparison of the completed-coefficient and constant-coefficient categories above.

proof.text: Construct the continuous-function coefficient sheaves, their quotient system and its actual limit. Forgetting commutativity preserves this sheafification, as the unit remains locally bijective. The tower category is Grothendieck abelian by the small-diagram theorem.

Construct scalar transitions through the normalized ordinary coefficient adjunction. Its section formula gives the transition on pure tensors; generation by local pure tensors proves naturality and uniqueness.

Use K-flat resolutions and scalar-extension invariance at each level. Exact scalar restriction and levelwise tower cohomology show that the ordinary tower construction preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. Apply the resolving-class derived-functor theorem, retaining its universal counit and triangulated structure.

Evaluate the specified balancing map on pure tensors. Naturality follows from the tensor formula for a module map. For the cocycle, compare both maps on triple pure tensors and use preservation of products and associativity. Repeated tensor-generation and the balancing isomorphism prove equality on the sheafified complexes.

Transport the homotopy derived counits to complex counits using the quotient factorization isomorphisms. Extend their composite and the natural balancing isomorphism by the right Kan universal property. On flat-term K-flat resolutions, scalar extension remains K-flat, so every counit in the composite is invertible. Resolution-wise extensionality proves invertibility and uniqueness on the full derived category.

The derived scalar-extension/restriction adjunction allows postcomposition of the scalar right Kan extension by derived restriction. Its ordinary target is the same complex functor as exact evaluation of the tower. Compare the two complex counits by that Kan property. Both are invertible on K-flat resolutions; resolution-wise extensionality gives the unique invertible natural transformation with exactly the specified evaluation formula.

In AdicCoefficientDatumCompleted, extend finiteCoefficientScalarMap uniquely across the locally bijective constant-ring unit by its W hom-equivalence. The extended sheaf map is locally bijective since its composite with the unit is, hence is an isomorphism; the same hom-equivalence proves its normalized uniqueness. Precompose the finite-coefficient naturality square by the unit. The normalized equations, naturality of sheafification, and the specified postcomposition formula for q identify both composites. The explicit completedConstant_quotients functor constructs the actual quotient tower from completedConstantQuotient and CompletedConstantQuotientTower of [def-weil-pbc-completed-constant-realization-data], with its level and transition equations. This is the elementary quotient-map construction, not an application of the downstream finite-complex realization theorem. Finally identify the ordinary scalar functor with the extension of an existing normalized scalar derived pair, using their object and map formulas and functor extensionality. Apply the proved preservation theorem for arbitrary K-flat complexes; no flat-term assumption is required.

S7 completes the six remaining interfaces of AdicCoefficientDatumCompleted. Use the existing normalized ordinary adjunction, scalar-transition existence, natural balancing maps and cocycle from the other realization of this same coefficient-datum node. The completedConstantExtension and reductionChange presentations are definitionally equal; use the latter consistently, and identify pure tensor sections by the same sheafification unit. Package the selected universal scalar derived pair with its counit, universal property and K-flat computation, retaining the standard localization. Apply the homotopy Hom compatibility theorem to obtain the normalized scalar adjunction. Its K-flat counit computation transports through the quotient-factorization isomorphisms to complexes. For the tower, choose K-flat resolutions, apply scalar-extension quasi-isomorphism invariance and exact restriction at each level, and use levelwise detection of tower quasi-isomorphisms. Derive this additive functor by the resolving-class theorem and transport the counit to complexes by the quotient universal property. Assemble scalar balancing maps into a natural isomorphism using their naturality; tensor-section uniqueness proves uniqueness, and the existing cocycle gives the reassociated equality. Keep the completed ring as the same actual inverse limit behind a locally irreducible definition and expose its projection naturality equation, preventing accidental unfolding of the chosen limit cone. For K-flat preservation, use scalarDerivedPair_exists from the normalized scalar adjunction realization. Its ordinary object and map formulas identify its extension with reductionChange by functor extensionality; transport scalarExtension_preservesKFlat along that equality. This avoids repeating the tensor-cancellation and total-complex construction.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a sheaf of rings $B_T$ on $T_{\Proet}$, define the Grothendieck abelian
category

$$
 \operatorname{Tow}_{B}(T)=
 \operatorname{Fun}\bigl(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},
              \Mod(T_{\Proet},B_T)\bigr).
$$

Its objects are strict inverse sequences $M_1\leftarrow M_2\leftarrow\cdots$,
and kernels, cokernels, and exactness are computed levelwise. Write
$\operatorname{ev}_n:\operatorname{Tow}_{B}(T)\to\Mod(T_{\Proet},B_T)$ for
the exact evaluation functor.

Let $A$ be noetherian, let $I=(a_1,\dots,a_r)$, assume $A/I$ is torsion, and
put $P_n=A/I^n$. Give $P_n$ the discrete topology and let $(P_n)_T$ be the
sheafification of

$$
 U\longmapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P_n)
$$

on $T_{\Proet}$. Define

$$
 A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T,
 \qquad
 D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\Mod(T_{\Proet},A_T)),
$$

and assume each $P_n$ is finite as a set and perfect as an $A$-module. For
$K\in D(T_{\Proet},A)$ choose a functorial K-flat representative $QK$ (in the
sense of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]). The strict complexes

$$
 QK\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T
$$

and the quotient maps $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ define an object $K_\bullet\in
D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. Its $n$-th evaluation is canonically

$$
 K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T,
$$

and it carries functorial normalization isomorphisms

$$
 K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n
$$

satisfying the quotient cocycle.
